chunk_findings.detail: `validate` only checks that a `family.unknown` row exists; it does not check that the row is empty. Given input such as `{"context_families.toml": {"sources": {"x": "..."}, "family": {"unknown": {"cache_kind": {"v": "explicit", "s": "verified", "src": "x", "d": "2024-01-01"}}}}, "context_harnesses.toml": {"harness": {}}}`, `validate` returns no problems, but `family_row(data, "gpt")` returns the `unknown` row and `usable` returns `"explicit"`. This lets an unknown model family be read as a verified fact, violating the stated invariant that `unknown` has no facts and is never read as true.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/context_families.py:validate

chunk_findings.detail: `validate` is documented to return one problem string per malformed fact/table, but `facts` assumes every row body is a mapping and calls `.items()` on it. For example, `validate({"context_families.toml": {"family": {"claude": "explicit"}}, "context_harnesses.toml": {"harness": {}}})` raises `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'items'` instead of reporting that the `claude` row is not a table. The same crash can propagate through `stale` and `doctor_notes` on malformed shipped data.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/context_families.py:facts

chunk_findings.detail: `[[REDACTED:host]]` presents local endpoints as a model family and marks its facts as supported by the vLLM APC page, but the note itself says `llama.cpp and Ollama: not read`. Given a local endpoint using llama.cpp or Ollama, line 81 returns `cache_kind.v="server_prefix"` with status `documented`, so the advisor can assume vLLM-style automatic prefix caching even though the cited source does not document that server. Line 82 is similarly unsupported: `read_mult` is marked `none` (“source documents the thing is absent”) from `vllm-apc`, but the APC page does not document the absence of per-token pricing for self-hosted endpoints. These facts should be restricted to vLLM or marked `unverified`/left out.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/context_families.toml:81

chunk_findings.detail: Several facts have machine-readable `v` values that are contradicted by their own source notes for models inside the same family. Line 32 gives Claude `read_mult.v=0.1`, while the note says `0.05 on Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5`; line 41 gives OpenAI `read_mult.v=0.1`, while the note says `0.05 on GPT-6.1 Sol and Terra`; line 55 gives DeepSeek `read_mult.v=0.02`, while the note computes `deepseek-v4-pro` as `0.033`. Given inputs such as `claude-sonnet-5.5`, `gpt-6.1`, or `deepseek-v4-pro`, a loader that reads `v` gets the wrong multiplier; the exceptions are only free-text notes, so the recorded facts are not accurate for models within the family.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/context_families.toml:32

chunk_findings.detail: The row encodes a known absence as an unstructured top-level `note`, not as a provenance-bearing fact. The file’s own contract says rows with no facts are an explicit unknown and every fact must be `{v, s, src, d, note?}`. The note says “compaction threshold not found (looked 2026-10-23); only a maxMode switch”, i.e. a dated observation that should be represented as a `window_knob` fact with `s = "none"` and `src = "window-note"`. If the advisor calls `facts("cursor")`, it sees no `window_knob` and therefore treats Cursor as unknown rather than verified-none, so it may still try to configure or probe a compaction threshold that the row says does not exist; if the top-level `note` is parsed as a fact, it also lacks the required `v`, `s`, `src`, and `d` fields.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/context_harnesses.toml:[harness.cursor]

chunk_findings.detail: The change’s intent says to “run and record the probes listed in research section 11,” and this file itself defines `verified` as “a probe executed on this machine.” But the file states “No probe below is `verified`” and later says live execution is “Not done, on purpose.” For the lines the intent calls out—hooks reaching subagents, PostCompact summary, Kimi cache, and compaction-cold cache write—the records are only WebFetch/vendor-page reads, not executed probe records. Thus the acceptance criterion for probe records is not satisfied as an executed probe record; the document is a research lead table, not the promised probe results.

chunk_findings.detail: Row #3 (“Does the compaction request write a cache entry when the cache is cold?”) has `Source, date` equal to only `none`, with no date. The intent requires every fact to have source and date, and the table header explicitly asks for a date. Even for an unresolved/open fact, the absence of a source/date prevents provenance and stale-age handling: a reader cannot tell when “not stated in any page read” was checked, so this row violates the provenance requirement for facts.
